sources_considered.why: Primary transparency research establishes broader company opacity and also documents improved disclosure.
A pre-post company research paper explicitly describes a neural-symbolic system and its methodological changes.
The December 2025 transparency assessment concerns a later state and does not identify the claimed pre-post causal effect.
Search surfaced a repository with later updates; its present contents cannot establish what was available by July 13, 2025.

evidence_items.publisher: Bommasani et al., TMLR; arXiv version
evidence_items.locator: Abstract, The 2024 Foundation Model Transparency Index
evidence_items.explanation: The audit documents substantial opacity but also an improvement in average transparency from 37 to 58 out of 100. It concerns foundation-model transparency generally and does not measure lost neurosymbolic research or establish that secrecy caused such a loss.

The AlphaGeometry2 paper explicitly describes its neural-symbolic predecessor and details changes to the language model, symbolic engine, formal language, and search. This is material evidence of company disclosure, although one disclosed system cannot establish the overall disclosure rate or eliminate research losses elsewhere.

unresolved_gaps: No defensible inventory establishes what fraction of attempted company neurosymbolic methods remained undisclosed.
The cited transparency audit does not measure neurosymbolic research specifically.
No cited study estimates the public research lost because of withholding, separately from technical difficulty or other constraints.
